body:
Vehicles regularly speed past the zebra crossing outside Hollins Primary School at the start and end of the day. Last month a child was nearly hit while crossing with her parents, and the crossing has no lights or warning signs.

Write a letter to the head of the council's road safety team.
bullets: give details of the times of day when the crossing is busiest
explain why parents are worried about the children's safety
ask the council to install lights and reduce the speed limit

body:
The empty plot behind the town library has been left unused for years and is now covered in rubbish. A group of residents would like to turn the site into a community garden where people can grow vegetables and flowers together.

Write a letter to the council's parks and open spaces officer.
bullets: introduce the residents' group and its aims
explain who would look after the garden and how it would be paid for
ask whether the council would allow the group to use the land

body:
The public toilets in the town square have been shut since March, and a sign says they are closed for repairs. No replacement facilities have appeared, and shoppers, older people and parents with young children now have nowhere to go while they are in the centre.

Write a letter to the council's street services manager.
bullets: ask what repairs are being carried out and why they are taking so long
explain how the closure affects shoppers and visitors
suggest a date by which the toilets should reopen

body:
Your local radio station has replaced its Saturday morning programme, which featured local musicians and community news, with a national show broadcast across the country. Many listeners in the area feel that the station has lost the local character that made it special.

Write a letter to the programme controller of the local radio station.
bullets: explain why the old programme mattered to local listeners
suggest how the station could keep local content alongside the national show
say whether you would keep listening if the change stays

body:
Your household recycling has not been collected on four of the last six scheduled days. Bins have been left overflowing in the street, and some neighbours have started putting recycling in the general waste, which is making the problem worse.

Write a letter to the waste collection service manager at the council.
bullets: give details of your usual collection day and the dates that were missed
say what effect this has had on your street
request a firm date for the next collection

body:
Your community group teaches English to adult migrants every week, but the room you have used for three years is now too small for the number of learners. You would like to book the council's community hall on Thursday evenings for a regular term.

Write a letter to the bookings officer at the council.
bullets: explain what the group does and who usually attends
give details of the days and times you need the hall
ask about the cost of a regular booking for a full term

body:
A local newspaper recently reported that the council plans to close the town's only public swimming pool at the end of the year. The article quoted no alternative for children's lessons or for older residents who rely on the pool for gentle exercise.

Write a letter to the editor of the newspaper.
bullets: explain why closing the pool would affect local families
ask what questions the paper should put to the council
propose that readers' views on the plans be published in a future edition

body:
The pavements on your street are covered in litter and fallen leaves, and the drains by the corner shop keep blocking after rain. You would like to organise a Saturday morning clean-up with the people who live nearby.

Write a letter to your neighbour.
bullets: explain why you want to organise the clean-up
suggest a time and a meeting point
ask whether they could bring gloves and bin bags

body:
The council has agreed to close your road for one afternoon in July so that residents can hold a street party. You would like your neighbour across the road to help with the planning, as she organised a successful event for her building last year.

Write a letter to your neighbour.
bullets: describe what you have already arranged
suggest which tasks she could take on
ask when she would be free to meet and discuss the plans

body:
You have run a stall selling handmade candles at the Saturday town market for two years. The market organiser has told you that your pitch will move to the far end of the car park, where far fewer shoppers walk past.

Write a letter to the market organiser.
bullets: explain how the move would affect your sales
ask whether the stall could return to its old position
suggest an alternative pitch that would suit the market

body:
Your employer gives every member of staff one paid volunteering day a year. You would like to use yours to help at a fundraising open day for a local wildlife rescue centre, but it falls in the same week as an important project deadline.

Write a letter to your manager.
bullets: give details of the open day and what you would be doing
explain how your work would be covered while you are away
offer to make up any lost time later in the month

body:
Your community choir has rehearsed in the back room of a pub for five years, but the landlord has said the room will be needed for private functions from next month. A church hall nearby may be free on Tuesday evenings.

Write a letter to the choir organiser.
bullets: give details of how much space the choir needs for rehearsals
suggest the church hall as a replacement
ask for a decision before the next rehearsal

body:
A few months ago you joined a volunteer group that meets every Sunday morning to clean up the riverside path. You were nervous at first, but you have made several new friends and you feel far more connected to the area where you live.

Write a letter to your friend.
bullets: tell them what the group has achieved so far
describe the best day you have spent with the volunteers
invite them to come along the next time they visit

body:
The first food festival in your town will take place in the market square next month, with stalls from local restaurants and live music in the evenings. Your friend moved away two years ago and has not been back since, so you would love her to visit.

Write a letter to your friend.
bullets: give details of the dates and what is on
suggest where she could stay during the weekend
ask when she might be able to arrive

body:
A friend of yours runs a charity book sale every spring to raise money for the local animal shelter. This year she is short of volunteers and has asked whether you could help on the Saturday of the sale.

Write a letter to your friend.
bullets: say which hours you could help on the Saturday
suggest someone else who might be willing to volunteer
offer an idea for attracting more buyers to the sale

body:
You have not been back to your hometown for three years, and a friend who now lives abroad has asked what has changed. A new shopping centre has opened near the station, and the old cinema on the high street has been turned into flats.

Write a letter to your friend.
bullets: describe the new shopping centre and what it offers
explain how local people have reacted to losing the cinema
tell them which of the old places you miss most

body:
You promised to help your friend launch a community reading group at the library next Tuesday, but a family emergency means you must cancel at very short notice. Your friend has already printed posters and invited several people to the first meeting.

Write a letter to your friend.
bullets: apologise for cancelling at such short notice
explain what happened without going into too much detail
suggest how you could still help with the first meeting
